extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and informed readers interested in the abc conjecture, inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT), and the Mochizuki–Scholze debate
extracted.subtask_description: A blog-post level commentary summarizing recent developments and reactions in the Mochizuki / IUT / abc-conjecture controversy, pointing to critiques, responses, and community reactions. Aimed at summarizing who found which arguments convincing and where attempted proofs run into trouble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful mathematical content
rubrics_metrics.description: "does not contain, at least from the point of view of the mathematics surrounding inter-universal Teichmüller theory, any meaningful mathematical content whatsoever."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mochizuki's report asserts that Joshi's series of preprints lack any meaningful mathematical content from the perspective of IUT. When evaluating a purported proof connected to IUT, check whether the work actually presents substantive mathematics rather than assertions or unsupported claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "conspicuously obvious to any reader of these preprints who is equipped with a solid, rigorous understanding of the actual mathematical content of inter-universal Teichmüller theory"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of IUT-related claims requires readers with a solid, rigorous understanding of IUT; non-experts are unlikely to be able to judge subtle technical points. Ensure evaluators have the appropriate background before treating a claim as credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to Scholze/Stix critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholze and Stix wrote a document explaining why the IUT proof strategy was flawed; Scholze later defended this argument in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any attempted proof or defense should directly and convincingly address the points raised in the Scholze/Stix critique. The blog points readers to those documents as the substantive record of the objections; lack of a clear rebuttal weakens credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community consensus / expert credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "virtually all experts in this subject have long ago given up on the idea that Mochizuki’s IUT theory has any hope of proving the abc conjecture."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight should be given to the consensus of domain experts when assessing the plausibility of high-profile proofs. Claims that run counter to broad expert judgement require especially strong, transparent evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical objections must be specifically identified and resolved (e.g., locality concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments point to precise places where Joshi's attempted proof runs into trouble; mentions of "locality" concerns and Scholze's MathOverflow note indicating precisely where Joshi's attempted proof runs into trouble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should identify concrete technical issues (such as locality problems) and check whether the purported proof gives explicit, correct resolutions. Vague rebuttals or minor edits that do not address the core technical points are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims of completing Mochizuki's proof require rigorous validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Joshi's preprints begin with the claim: "This paper completes (in Theorem 7.1.1) the remarkable proof of the abc-conjecture announced by Shinichi Mochizuki..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a paper claims to complete or vindicate another mathematician's announced proof, readers should verify both that the claimed dependencies are correctly used and that the new work stands up to detailed scrutiny by experts; such strong claims demand strong evidence.
